issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a method addGuestStudents(int) that accepts a single int parameter, and the solution implements public void addGuestStudents(int). However, the template Lecture.java declares addGuestStudents with a different signature: addGuestStudents(int, boolean). This parameter mismatch can confuse students about the correct method signature to implement and may cause inconsistencies with automated tests or the expected solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template method signature to match the specification and solution: change public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). If input validation is desired, provide an overloaded helper method or include validation internally without changing the public signature described in the problem statement.

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution implement an addGuestStudents method with a single int parameter (addGuestStudents(int)), but the template Lecture class provides a stub with a different signature that includes an extra boolean parameter (addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput)). This mismatch in the method signature creates a mapping barrier: students reading the exercise will expect to implement or use addGuestStudents(int) as specified, but the provided template forces a different signature, which can cause confusion and compile/test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to match the problem statement and solution: declare public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... } and perform any validation internally if needed. This aligns template, problem description, and reference solution.
